Neha / team — filling in details below for the RFI and callers' questions. I'll prepare a short memo for procurement. Key points to call out:

1) Subprocessor list (current, as of 2026-03-06):
   - Amazon Web Services (primary cloud, us-east-1, eu-west-1) — compute, object storage
   - Google Cloud (europe-west-1) — optional inference replica for low-latency EU-region customers
   - FastKV Inc (KV cache service) — hosted in us-east-1
   - LogsNow (logging/metrics vendor) — US-hosted, SOC 2 Type II
   - TranscribeCo (optional speech ↔ text) — hosted EU/US depending on contract

   Note: For Greenstone GLBA workloads we recommend Dedicated (reserved capacity) or Private (VPC) to avoid multi-tenant co-residency.

2) Transfer mechanism: Redwood offers Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) for controller-controller and controller-processor flows where applicable; we also support Data Processing Addendums that reference SCCs. Currently we do not rely on an EU adequacy decision for transfers to our US-hosted inference clusters unless the customer pins EU-only deployment.

3) Customer-managed keys: Supported in Private deployments via KMS integration (AWS KMS / GCP KMS) and HSM options for enterprise tiers. Note that customer-managed keys in hosted (multi-tenant) mode have limitations; recommend Private for KMS-bound use cases.

4) GLBA/vertical addendum feasibility:
   - We have a GLBA-ready addendum template used in one customer pilot (banking division) — includes controls around data segregation, audit logs, and restricted access.
   - Open items: 1) whether Greenstone requires on-prem HSM for key storage; 2) whether customer data classification includes account numbers / SSNs in prompts (we need the scope).

I'll fill the RFI spreadsheet and attach the completed CSV + a short memo with recommended path (SCCs + Dedicated/Private + KMS).

— Kar
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security | Redwood Inference
